Hidden leak, wet yard or a water bill that won't come down? SRQ Leak Pros connects Sarasota homeowners with independent local pros who find leaks and fix water service lines.

Quick answer: Leak detection in Sarasota, FL means finding a hidden leak without tearing up your home or yard. A local pro uses meter tests, acoustic listening, tracer gas and thermal cameras to pinpoint the spot. The EPA says household leaks waste more than 9,300 gallons a year in the average home.

Most leaks in Sarasota hide where you can't see them. They sit in the buried water service line between the meter and the house, in copper pipes under a slab floor, in a cracked sewer lateral, or in pool plumbing. The first sign is often a bill that jumps, a soggy patch of lawn, or the sound of running water when every tap is off.

Why leak detection in Sarasota, FL is its own job

Sarasota's homes and soil make leaks behave in local ways. Knowing them helps you explain the problem on the phone and judge the answers you get.

  • Slab homes are the norm. Many Sarasota houses sit on a concrete slab foundation with water lines underneath. A leak there can run for months before it shows.
  • Sandy soil drains fast. A broken service line can soak into sand and never surface, so the only clue is the meter.
  • The water table can be shallow. Near the bay and the Gulf, wet ground is normal, which makes a yard leak harder to spot by eye.
  • Pipe age varies by block. Older neighborhoods may still have galvanized steel, cast iron sewer pipe or early copper. Homes from the late 1970s to the 1990s may have polybutylene.
  • Pools are everywhere. Pool plumbing adds hundreds of feet of buried pipe to many lots.

Sarasota County's own leak FAQ notes that the county looks after more than 104,000 service lines and over 1,400 miles of water mains. Its field crews decide whether a reported leak is the county's job or the customer's. On private property, the repair and the leak detection belong to the owner, as county officials told ABC7 Sarasota in July 2026.

How a leak is found, step by step

A good leak pro works from the simplest test to the most precise. A typical visit follows this order:

  1. Meter test. With every fixture off, the pro watches the meter's flow indicator. If it moves, water is escaping somewhere.
  2. Isolation. Closing the main shut-off and other valves splits the system into sections. This tells the pro whether the leak is in the yard, under the slab or inside the walls.
  3. Pressure test. A gauge on a hose bib or line shows whether pressure holds or drops.
  4. Pinpointing. Acoustic ground microphones, tracer gas, line locating and infrared cameras narrow the leak to a small spot.
  5. Repair plan. You get options, such as a spot repair, a reroute or a full line replacement, with the trade-offs explained.

What affects the cost of leak detection and repair

No honest price can be set before someone looks at the leak. These factors move the price most:

FactorWhy it matters
Where the leak isA yard leak is often easier to reach than one under a slab or a driveway.
How it is foundA quick meter and pressure test costs less than a full tracer-gas search.
The repair methodA spot repair, a reroute and a full replacement differ a lot in labor.
Pipe material and lengthCopper, PEX, CPVC and HDPE cost different amounts, and longer runs cost more.
Surface restorationConcrete, pavers, tile and landscaping may need to be put back.
PermitsLine replacements usually need a local permit and an inspection.

For national price ranges from a named source, see the guides on water line replacement cost and slab leak repair cost. Always ask for a written estimate.

Warning signs of a hidden leak

Call a leak pro if you notice any of these:

  • Your water bill rises with no change in use
  • The meter's flow indicator moves when all water is off
  • A patch of lawn stays green, soft or soggy in dry weather
  • Water pools near the meter box or along the driveway
  • A floor feels warm in one spot, or you hear water running
  • Low water pressure in every fixture at once
  • Cracks in tile or baseboards that are damp or stained
  • A pool loses more than normal evaporation

Leak detection questions

How do I know if I have a leak in my water line?

Turn off every faucet and appliance, then look at the water meter. If the small flow indicator is moving, water is leaving the system somewhere. A soggy yard, a rising bill or low pressure everywhere are other common clues.

Who pays to fix a leak between the meter and my house?

In Sarasota County, leaks on private property are the owner's job. The utility handles its side of the meter and the main. Read who is responsible for the water line for details.

Can a leak be found without digging up my yard or floor?

Usually, yes. Acoustic listening, tracer gas, line locating and thermal imaging can narrow a leak to a small area. Digging is then limited to that spot, or the pro may suggest a reroute instead.

Is SRQ Leak Pros a plumbing company?

No. SRQ Leak Pros is a referral service. Your call is connected with an independent local provider, who quotes, performs and bills for the work.

Should the provider hold a Florida license?

Florida law treats water and sewer line work as plumbing contractor work. Ask for the provider's license number and check it on the state's DBPR license search before work begins.

What areas around Sarasota are covered?

Calls from the City of Sarasota and nearby areas such as Venice, Osprey, Nokomis, North Port, Siesta Key, Longboat Key, Lakewood Ranch and Bradenton can be connected with local providers.

Do I need to call 811 before a leak repair?

Florida law requires a call to Sunshine 811 at least two full business days before digging. A provider doing the excavation normally handles this, but confirm it before any digging starts.
